method: Every level is entered in dBFS and converted to a linear amplitude with A = 10^(dBFS / 20), so a -60 dBFS harmonic is 0.001 of full scale. The harmonic amplitudes are combined in quadrature, which is the RMS sum of unrelated tones: the distortion residual D is the square root of the sum of the squares of the entered harmonics. THD is D divided by the fundamental amplitude, shown as a percentage and as a level in dB relative to the fundamental, so a single harmonic 60 dB down gives 0.1% and -60 dB. THD+N adds the noise floor to the same quadrature sum, so it is never smaller than THD and the two agree when no noise floor is entered. SINAD is the fundamental amplitude divided by that combined residual, expressed in decibels, and it is the arithmetic inverse of THD+N in dB. Effective number of bits follows from SINAD as (SINAD - 1.76) / 6.02, where 1.76 dB is the peak-to-RMS offset of a full-scale sine and 6.02 dB is the dynamic range of one bit; the result is the resolution of an ideal converter with the same SINAD and is not a claim about a real device. The residual is also reported as an absolute dBFS level. The per-harmonic breakdown gives each harmonic's share of the distortion energy and marks the dominant one. Each harmonic from the second to the seventh is optional and blank means absent, at least one harmonic or a noise floor must be entered, and every level is limited to -160 to 0 dBFS with up to two decimals. Because a harmonic at or above the fundamental gives distortion above 100%, that case is reported as a warning rather than silently accepted as a device measurement. Everything runs in the browser with no uploads, network access or storage.

sources.title: Total harmonic distortion is the RMS sum of the harmonic amplitudes divided by the fundamental amplitude, quoted as a percentage or as a level below the fundamental.
SINAD is the fundamental amplitude divided by the RMS sum of all other spectral components, harmonics plus noise, expressed in decibels.
ENOB follows from SINAD as (SINAD - 1.76 dB) / 6.02 dB for a full-scale sine, where 1.76 dB is the peak-to-RMS offset and 6.02 dB is one bit of dynamic range.
AES17-2015, AES standard for digital audio engineering: measurement of audio equipment, for the THD+N convention of measuring the residual with the fundamental notched out.
